bottom_line: In patients stabilised after an acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban versus placebo did not significantly reduce the primary efficacy endpoint (HR 0.79 [0.60–1.05]).
implications: These data support that, versus placebo, rivaroxaban increased clinically significant bleeding in a dose-dependent manner (eg, HR 5.06 [3.45–7.42] for 20 mg) while the primary efficacy endpoint was not statistically different (HR 0.79 [0.60–1.05], p=0.10). The numbers do support a reduction in the main secondary endpoint of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (HR 0.69 [0.50–0.96], p=0.0270), but the document also states the trial was not powered for efficacy.

major_points.text: Phase II, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial across 297 sites in 27 countries (n=3491).
major_points.quote: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II, dose-escalation study, 3491 participants were randomised at 297 sites in 27 countries.

major_points.text: Randomisation was stratified by investigator decision to use aspirin only vs aspirin plus a thienopyridine, and assigned 1:1:1 to placebo or rivaroxaban once daily vs twice daily.
major_points.quote: Participants were randomised within each strata and dose tier with a block randomisation method at 1:1:1 to receive either placebo or rivaroxaban (at doses 5–20 mg) given once daily or the same total daily dose given twice daily.

major_points.text: Primary safety endpoint was clinically significant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention).
major_points.quote: The primary safety endpoint was clinically signiﬁcant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention)

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or severe recurrent ischaemia requiring revascularisation during 6 months.
major_points.quote: the primary eﬃcacy endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or severe recurrent ischaemia requiring revascularisation during 6 months.

major_points.text: The primary efficacy endpoint was numerically lower with rivaroxaban vs placebo but not statistically significant.
major_points.quote: Rates of the primary eﬃcacy endpoint were 5·6% (126/2331) for rivaroxaban versus 7·0% (79/1160) for placebo (HR 0·79 [0·60–1·05], p=0·10).

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban reduced the main secondary endpoint (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) versus placebo.
major_points.quote: Rivaroxaban reduced the main secondary eﬃcacy endpoint of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke compared with placebo (87/2331 [3·9%] vs 62/1160 [5·5%]; HR 0·69, [95% CI 0·50–0·96], p=0·0270).

absolute_effects.text: Primary efficacy endpoint: 5.6% (126/2331) for rivaroxaban vs 7.0% (79/1160) for placebo.
absolute_effects.quote: Rates of the primary eﬃcacy endpoint were 5·6% (126/2331) for rivaroxaban versus 7·0% (79/1160) for placebo

absolute_effects.text: Most common adverse event: chest pain 248/2309 [10.7%] vs 118/1153 [10.2%].
absolute_effects.quote: The most common adverse event in both groups was chest pain (248/2309 [10·7%] vs 118/1153 [10·2%]).

absolute_effects.text: Clinically significant bleeding (pooled placebo vs rivaroxaban 20 mg): 3.3% (37/1153) vs 16.0% (47/301) once daily.

subgroups.text: For the primary efficacy endpoint, hazard ratio differed between stratum 1 and stratum 2 (interaction p=0.034).
subgroups.quote: Compared with placebo, rivaroxaban was associated with an HR of 0·53 (95% CI 0·33–0·84) for death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or severe recurrent ischaemia requiring revascularisation in stratum 1 and an HR of 0·99 (0·69–1·42) in stratum 2 (p for inter- action=0·034).

subgroups.text: Exploratory interactions were noted by age and index event.
subgroups.quote: In exploratory analyses, signiﬁcant interactions were noted on the basis of age (p for interaction=0·007) and index event (p for inter- action=0·042).

harms.text: One fatal bleed occurred (intracranial haemorrhage) in rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily group of stratum 1.
harms.quote: One fatal bleed occurred: a participant in the rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily dose group of stratum 1 presented with an intracranial haemorrhage.

harms.text: Most common adverse event in both groups was chest pain.
harms.quote: The most common adverse event in both groups was chest pain (248/2309 [10·7%] vs 118/1153 [10·2%]).

harms.text: In stratum 2, 347 discontinued study drug in rivaroxaban group vs 149 in placebo group.
harms.quote: 347 discontinued study drug                  149 discontinued study drug

inclusion_criteria.text: Randomisation occurred 1–7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Randomisation occurred 1–7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.

inclusion_criteria.text: Symptoms suggestive of an acute coronary syndrome that lasted at least 10 min at rest.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Participants were required to have symptoms suggestive of an acute coronary syndrome that lasted at least 10 min at rest

inclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosis of ST-elevation myocardial infarction or diagnosis of non-STEMI or unstable angina with at least one qualifying feature.
inclusion_criteria.quote: either a diagnosis of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or a diagnosis of non-STEMI or unstable angina with at least one of the following: raised cardiac enzyme markers, 1 mm or more ST-segment deviation, or a TIMI risk score of 3 or more.

exclusion_criteria.quote: Major exclusion criteria were a haemoglobin concentration less than 100 g/L

exclusion_criteria.text: Platelet count less than 90 000 per μL of blood.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Major exclusion criteria were a haemoglobin concentration less than 100 g/L, a platelet count less than 90 000 per μL of blood
Major exclusion criteria were a haemoglobin concentration less than 100 g/L, a platelet count less than 90 000 per μL of blood, or a history of any intracranial haemorrhage.

exclusion_criteria.text: Planned percutaneous coronary intervention within 30 days of randomisation.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or had planned percutaneous coronary intervention within 30 days of randomisation

exclusion_criteria.text: Renal dysfunction (creatinine clearance <30 mL per min).
exclusion_criteria.quote: renal dysfunction (creatinine clearance <30 mL per min)

exclusion_criteria.text: Life expectancy of less than 6 months.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or a life expectancy of less than 6 months.

analysis_methods.text: Safety analyses included participants who received at least one dose of study drug; efficacy analyses were intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: Safety analyses included all participants who received at least one dose of study drug; eﬃcacy analyses were by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: Baseline characteristics compared using Wilcoxon rank sum test or t test for continuous variables, and χ² test for categorical variables.
analysis_methods.quote: Baseline characteristics were compared with the Wilcoxon rank sum test or t test for continuous variables and the χ² test for categorical variables.

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratios and 95% CIs from Cox proportional hazards regression models; stratified log-rank used for comparisons vs pooled placebo.
analysis_methods.quote: Hazard ratios and 95% CIs were calculated on the basis of Cox proportional hazards regression models. The log-rank test, stratiﬁed by stratum 1 and stratum 2, was used to compare each treatment group to the pooled (ie, entire) placebo group.

analysis_methods.text: Sample size of at least 225 patients per dose tier and stratum chosen to estimate bleeding rate for each treatment.
analysis_methods.quote: The sample size of at least 225 patients per dose tier and stratum was chosen to provide an estimate of the bleeding rate for each treatment.

trial_conduct.quote: This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00402597.

trial_conduct.text: Blinded clinical events committee adjudicated all components of the main safety and efficacy endpoints.
trial_conduct.quote: A blinded clinical events committee adjudicated all the components of the main safety and eﬃcacy endpoints.

trial_conduct.text: Independent data monitoring committee was in place.
trial_conduct.quote: Independent data monitoring committee D Weaver (chairperson), A Skene (independent statistician), C Hamm.

trial_conduct.text: Participants were seen every 30 days; liver function tests were done every month.
trial_conduct.quote: Participants were seen every 30 days, and were to be treated for 6 months (180 days).

criticisms.text: The trial was not powered to obtain a significant effect for efficacy (and states it was not powered for efficacy).
criticisms.quote: Although the eﬃcacy of rivaroxaban compared with placebo was also assessed, this trial was not powered to obtain a signiﬁcant eﬀect.

criticisms.text: Many active treatment groups and some dosing strategies assessed in only a small number of patients, limiting certainty for individual dosing strategies.
criticisms.quote: some individual dosing strategies were assessed in only a small number of patients. Consequently, in assessment of individual dosing strategies, whether some observations are due to chance or pathobiology is unclear

criticisms.text: Overall primary efficacy endpoint results require careful interpretation due to heterogeneity between strata 1 and 2.
criticisms.quote: In consideration of the heterogeneity between strata 1 and 2, the overall results pertaining to the primary eﬃcacy endpoint need careful interpretation.
